T2 Short vs Full T2

Which of the two corporate return forms a quiet year uses, what the eight conditions decide, and the six things that are identical either way.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOWCheck the Eight Conditions

Quick Answer

Both are the same return at the same price. The T2 Short is a two-page version of the T2 that a corporation may use only where it meets every one of the Canada Revenue Agency’s eight conditions for the short return. Where one condition fails, the full T2 is the return instead. Either way the filing is $300.00 plus HST per tax year, carries the same schedules, is signed on the same Form T183CORP and is transmitted the same way.

Nil T2 filing in Canada › Nil T2 filing cost › T2 Short vs Full T2

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Last reviewed: November 4, 2026

Two Forms, One Return

The T2 Short is not a lighter obligation or a cheaper service. It is a shorter version of the same corporate income tax return, and a corporation either qualifies to use it or does not. Nothing about the decision is ours to make and nothing about it changes what you pay.

That is the whole answer, and it is worth stating plainly because the form is often discussed as though choosing it were a strategy. It is not a choice. The eight conditions decide it, and where one of them fails we file the full return at the same fee rather than a different one.

This comparison sets two of our own filing routes against each other and names no other provider. Where a comparison on this site does name one, it states that provider’s published prices and published features only.

The Eight Conditions Decide It

A corporation may use the short return only where every one of these holds for the tax year:

  • The corporation is a Canadian-controlled private corporation throughout the tax year.
  • It has nil net income, or a loss, for income tax purposes this year.
  • It has one permanent establishment only.
  • It paid no taxable dividends and received none in the year.
  • It reports in Canadian currency.
  • It is claiming no refundable credits.
  • It has no Ontario transitional tax debit.
  • It has no amount calculated under section 34.2.

Meeting seven of the eight is not enough. One condition failing puts the corporation on the full return, which we file at the same fee rather than a different one.

The T2 Short eligibility checker tests all eight at once, the exclusion checker names which one excludes you, and the CCPC condition checker takes the first condition on its own.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Same Work Either Way

Whichever form the conditions point to, the return is prepared, reviewed and transmitted the same way, at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Reviewed by a CPA

Either form is prepared and reviewed by a CPA Ontario member before it is transmitted. The review does not get shorter because the form does.

The schedules are inside the fee

GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141, Schedule 24 on a first return, Schedule 50, Schedule 8 and loss continuity, on whichever form applies.

Transmitted and confirmed

Transmitted electronically by a registered EFILE electronic filer, with your CRA confirmation emailed within 3 business days.

A corporation with a December 31 year-end and no activity in the year

Its return is due the following June 30 on either form. Say it holds share capital from incorporation and a small bank balance, and nothing moved: the GIFI schedules are required because something sits on the books, Schedule 50 lists its sole shareholder, and the fee is $300.00 plus HST per tax year. If all eight conditions hold, that return goes on the two-page short form. If the corporation received a dividend, two conditions fail at once, the full return is used, and the year is no longer a nil year at all. The figures here illustrate how the rules apply and are not drawn from a client file.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the T2 Short cheaper than the full T2?

No. Both are $300.00 plus HST per tax year. The T2 Short is included in the fee where a corporation qualifies for it rather than charged separately, and where it does not qualify we file the full return at the same fee.

Can I choose to file the T2 Short?

It is not a choice. A corporation may use the short return only where it meets every one of the eight conditions. Meeting seven is not enough, and we check all eight before the return is prepared.

What is actually different between the two forms?

Two things: which corporations may use it, and how long the form is. The deadline, the schedules, Form T183CORP, the filing route and the confirmation are the same on both.

Does the short form mean fewer schedules?

No. The schedules are decided by what sits on the corporation’s books and by whether it is a first return, not by which form carries them. A quiet corporation holding share capital still files GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 either way.

Which condition fails most often?

A dividend paid or received, and not being a Canadian-controlled private corporation throughout the year. Both also mean the year is not a nil year for this service, so they decide more than the form.

Who decides which form my return goes on?

The eight conditions do, tested against your corporation before the return is prepared. The T2 Short eligibility checker runs the same test you can run yourself.

What does CCPC throughout the tax year mean?

The corporation has to be a Canadian-controlled private corporation for every day of the year, not merely on the last day. A change of control partway through the year breaks the condition even where the corporation looks the same at the year-end.

Does a loss year still qualify for the T2 Short?

Yes. The condition is nil net income or a loss for income tax purposes, so a loss does not fail it. The loss still has to be reported and carried forward correctly, which is work the fee covers on either form.

What counts as a permanent establishment?

Broadly, a fixed place of business. The condition is that the corporation has one only. A corporation operating in two provinces generally has more than one, fails the condition and goes on the full return.

Does receiving a dividend disqualify the T2 Short?

Yes, and it does more than that. A taxable dividend received fails the condition outright, and it also means the year is not a nil year for this service at all.

Does paying a dividend disqualify it?

Yes. The condition covers taxable dividends both paid and received, so either direction fails it and the full return is used instead.

What if the corporation reports in a currency other than Canadian dollars?

The condition is that the corporation reports in Canadian currency. A corporation that has elected a functional currency fails it and files the full return.

What is a refundable credit for this purpose?

A credit the corporation can be paid out even where it owes no tax. Claiming one fails the condition. A genuinely quiet corporation usually claims nothing at all, so this condition rarely decides the form on its own.

What is the Ontario transitional tax debit?

A legacy Ontario amount arising from the move to federal administration of Ontario corporate tax. Where a corporation has one, the short return cannot be used. Most corporations incorporated since that transition do not.

What is an amount calculated under section 34.2?

An income adjustment for a corporation that is a member of a partnership with a different fiscal period. Where such an amount applies, the short return cannot be used.

Does the number of shareholders affect eligibility?

Not directly. None of the eight conditions counts shareholders. The shareholder list affects Schedule 50, which is required on either form for every shareholder holding 10 per cent or more.

Does a corporation with no bank account qualify?

Having no bank account does not fail any of the eight conditions. What the corporation holds affects which schedules are filed, not which form carries them.

Can a corporation that has never traded use the T2 Short?

Yes, where the eight conditions hold. A corporation that never began operating still owes a return for each tax year since incorporation, and each of those years is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Which schedules does a quiet corporation actually file?

Commonly GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141, Schedule 50 where a shareholder holds 10 per cent or more, and Schedule 24 on a first return. Loss continuity is added where there is a loss to carry. The list is the same on either form.

Why is Schedule 100 required if nothing happened?

Schedule 100 is the balance sheet. A corporation that issued shares at incorporation has share capital sitting on its books whether or not it traded, so there is a balance sheet to report even in a year with no activity.

When is Schedule 24 required?

On a first return. It carries the first-time filer information, and it is required on the first return whichever form that return goes on.

When is Schedule 50 required?

Where a shareholder holds 10 per cent or more of any class of shares. A single-shareholder corporation is over that threshold by definition, so it files Schedule 50 on either form.

Does the T2 Short include Schedule 8?

Schedule 8 is capital cost allowance. It is filed where the corporation has depreciable property, on either form. A corporation holding nothing but share capital and a bank balance normally has none.

Do the schedules cost extra?

No. Every schedule the corporation needs is inside $300.00 plus HST per tax year, on whichever form applies.

When is the return due on either form?

Six months after the fiscal year-end, the same on both. A December 31 year-end is due the following June 30.

Is the deadline different for the short form?

No. The form the return goes on does not move the deadline. Only the fiscal year-end sets it.

Can the T2 Short be filed on paper?

We transmit every return electronically as a registered EFILE electronic filer, and your confirmation is emailed within 3 business days. Whether a particular corporation is permitted to file on paper is a separate question and does not change which form its return goes on.

How is Form T183CORP signed?

An authorized signing officer signs Form T183CORP before the return is transmitted. That requirement is identical on both forms, and nothing is sent to the Canada Revenue Agency until it is signed.

How long until the confirmation arrives?

Your CRA confirmation is emailed within 3 business days of transmission, on either form.

Does the form affect how the return is reviewed?

No. Either form is prepared and reviewed by a CPA Ontario member before transmission. The review follows the corporation’s facts, not the length of the form.

Can past years be filed on the T2 Short?

Yes, where the eight conditions held in that year. Eligibility is tested year by year against the facts of that year, not against the corporation as it stands today.

What if one year qualifies and another does not?

Each year goes on the form its own facts point to, so a corporation can file one year on the short return and the next on the full return. Every quiet year is $300.00 plus HST per tax year either way.

Does switching forms between years cause a problem?

No. The returns are filed year by year and the Canada Revenue Agency assesses each on its own. A year on the full return does not oblige the following year to use it.

Is the price different if several years are filed at once?

No. The fee is $300.00 plus HST per tax year, counted per year, however many years are filed together.

Which checker should I run first?

The T2 Short eligibility checker tests all eight at once. Where it returns not eligible, the exclusion checker names the condition that did it.
